post.title: Elder theft's most common suspects: adult children
post.ig:
In bank reports, adult children were the most common elder-theft suspects (FinCEN, 2024).

FinCEN reviewed 155,415 reports filed June 2022-June 2023: about $27B in suspected elder financial exploitation. When the victim knew the suspect, theft averaged $98,863 per report (median $23,762).
A power of attorney lets an agent handle someone's money; agents must act in good faith and in the person's best interest.
Red flags: sudden big withdrawals, new names on accounts, unpaid bills, a helper who won't let them speak for themselves.
National Elder Fraud Hotline: 1-833-372-8311.

Sources: FinCEN (2024); Uniform Power of Attorney Act; CFPB; U.S. DOJ.
News and education, not financial or legal advice.
